title: TriSAR-3D and PaintFusion: A Novel Trimodal LiDAR-RGB-Thermal Dataset and Method for 3D Person Detection in Search and Rescue

problem.summary: In search-and-rescue robotics, the objective of a mission is often to locate people in the scene, which may be indoors or outdoors, under lighting conditions that range from daylight to complete darkness. 3D detection models can contribute to such missions.

solution.summary: This section describes the trimodal sensor-box, the calibration of the LiDAR, RGB, and thermal sensors, and the proposed early-fusion 3D detection network.

components: Sensor-box For data acquisition, we use a custom sensor-box that integrates an Ouster OS0 LiDAR, a FLIR A70 thermal camera, and an Intel RealSense D455 RGB-D camera (Fig. 4).
The LiDAR is mounted on top of the frame to minimize occlusions caused by the frame structure.
It provides a vertical field of view (FoV) of 90◦ with 128 channels (0.7◦ angular resolution), a horizontal resolution of 1024 (0.35◦ ), a rotation rate of 20 Hz, and a maximum range of 250 m.
